We are small, run properly, and our bookkeeping is handled by an external firm. What we do not have is a finance professional who owns the output.
Right now the CEO does all of the finance: the monthly close, five indirect tax regimes, the pricing analysis, the landed cost, the advisor coordination. It works, and it does not scale, and there is no one else who could pick it up.
You would take that. Not the bookkeeping - an external firm does the bookkeeping. The layer above it: whether the numbers are right, whether the filings are on time, and whether someone other than the founder can read the business.
This is a build-and-run role in a business that has never had one. You will inherit real processes that mostly work and real gaps that do not. You bring the analysis and the judgement; the CEO keeps the final call on pricing, payments, tax and structure.
What you would own

•
The monthly close. You own the calendar, the quality bar and the query queue while the external bookkeeper does the execution. Settlement reconciliation for two marketplace accounts, the consolidated group P&L across both entities, the stock take, and the year-end pack for our Australian tax advisors. Getting the close to business day five is a first-half objective, not a week-one expectation.

•
Indirect tax in five jurisdictions. US sales tax, German VAT, UK VAT under Making Tax Digital, Canadian GST, Australian BAS. Four external firms do the filings. You are not expected to have technical depth in all five regimes - nobody does. You run the control that sits over them: a filing calendar nobody misses, data prepared to each firm's specification, a reconciliation of what was filed against what the books say, and a written query log when the two disagree.

•
Management reporting. Daily channel P&L across both marketplace accounts, a weekly sales report, a monthly P&L analysis with an executive summary someone acts on, the KPI scorecard, product and range performance. Today these exist in pieces; you would make them one thing.

•
Pricing and unit economics. The standing price review, margin verification after every price change, markdowns on aged stock, contribution by channel, third-party logistics cost against what we are charged. You bring the analysis; the CEO decides.

•
Landed cost. A monthly reference refresh and verification of cost uploads. Cost rolls forward in our systems, so an error corrupts forward margin silently and nothing tells you. There is a backlog of known cost conflicts to work through in your first half-year.

•
Controls and documentation. A written SOP for every recurring process, an access map so the function survives any one person being unavailable, and an audit-readiness file that does not exist today. These are gating deliverables, not nice-to-haves.

Not in this role
Payment release stays with the CEO. Accounts payable processing and payroll preparation stay where they are today, with our EA and the external bookkeeper, so your time goes to the close, the tax control, the reporting and the analysis. title: Senior Applied Scientist - AI Platform
description:
AI Platform builds the foundations of Datadog's AI efforts. The org is 70+ people organised in three pillars: training and serving (GPU clusters, distributed training, low-level infrastructure), agents (agent harnesses, memory systems, the internal AI gateway that routes every LLM request at Datadog), and evaluation and experimentation. This role sits in the evaluation and experimentation pillar, which owns Datadog's shared annotation and evaluation infrastructure - including the evaluation scenario store and the telemetry archival systems used across the Bits org. Together they let an agent travel back in time and query what Datadog looked like at the exact moment an incident happened, so scenarios can be replayed and agent performance tracked over time.

Specifically, you'll be the first applied scientist on GenSim (Generative Simulations), the team that builds the environments Datadog's agents learn in. GenSim doesn't replay sampled telemetry - it stands up real, fully instrumented applications that talk to Datadog, drives them with representative traffic, injects controlled failures, and records what happens. title: Director / Senior Director, Intellectual Property, Life Sciences
locationText: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is building an autonomous scientific platform and applying it across therapeutics, materials, and other scientific domains. Our life sciences programs run from early research through candidate selection, often in collaboration with external partners, which makes strong intellectual property work essential.

We are looking for a life sciences patent lawyer to own IP strategy for these programs end to end. This is not a docket-management role. You will decide what gets filed and how it is claimed, and you will help shape the IP positions that support our commercial agreements.

The work spans both halves of a life sciences IP practice that are often split between two people: building and prosecuting a global patent portfolio, and advising on the IP terms of collaborations, licensing, and financings. If you have done both and want to do them for a single company rather than a client list, this role is built for you.

You will be the senior life sciences voice on a small, high-leverage team, with real scope to build.

What You'll Be Building

• Own global patent strategy for therapeutic programs, including composition-of-matter, formulation, delivery, method-of-use, and platform claims.

• Direct outside counsel on drafting and prosecution across major jurisdictions; set claim strategy rather than relay it.

• Design claim architecture that protects programs at each stage of their life cycle.

• Lead patentability, validity, and freedom-to-operate analyses; translate findings into go/no-go and design-around recommendations.

• Serve as IP lead on collaboration, option, license, and services agreements, including the IP terms that follow from them.

• Run IP due diligence for financings and partner transactions, including portfolio schedules, chain of title, and license obligations.

• Advise on inbound licenses for third-party software, data, models, and research tools, and build the clearance process that supports compliant use.

• Mentor junior legal team members and, over time, build and manage the life sciences IP function.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• J.D. and active bar admission, with USPTO registration.

• 12+ years of substantive patent experience in the life sciences, in a law firm, in-house, or a combination.

• Technical degree in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular or cellular biology, immunology, or a closely related field.

• Demonstrated ownership of global patent portfolios for biopharmaceutical products, with direct responsibility for claim strategy.

• Experience across a range of therapeutic modalities.

• Track record producing patentability, validity, and FTO assessments that supported real business decisions.

• Experience advising on IP aspects of collaborations, licensing, acquisitions, or financings, including diligence and negotiating provisions.

Bonus Points For

• Experience with option-based or milestone-based collaboration structures.

• Experience maintaining portfolio positions across related programs and partners.

• Familiarity with structure-based similarity and analog definitions as used in contracts.

• Experience with PTAB post-grant proceedings or district court and ITC litigation support.

• Exposure to AI or computational drug discovery, including related inventorship questions.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

description:
ABOUT SENTRY

Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building.

Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll join the team behind Sentry’s Size Analysis and Snapshots, two products that check every pull request before it ships. Size Analysis breaks down iOS and Android builds to explain why an app got bigger. Snapshots catches unintended visual changes by diffing screenshots against a baseline. Both run in our customers’ CI, report straight to Source Code Management providers, and handle some of the heaviest payloads at Sentry: multi-GB app binaries and builds with tens of thousands of images.

IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

You’ll work full-stack with a backend lean, owning features from the moment a build arrives from CI, to the moment when UI engineers use that data to decide whether to merge. You’ll own the codebase behind our mobile binary analysis and large-scale image comparison. You’ll share the pipeline, the GitHub integration and on-call with the rest of the Sentry team.

- Extend our product: own the functionality end-to-end, react on feedback and come up with proposals for further product development.

- Own the GitHub integration end to end: PR status checks, comments, approvals and webhooks, including races, duplicates and missing-baseline edge cases

- Ship frontend features such as treemaps, build comparisons and diff viewers that stay fast on huge datasets

- Run what you build: deploys across regions, metrics, logging and on-call, and be the person who debugs the weird customer build

YOU’LL LOVE THIS JOB IF YOU

- Want your work to show up in the pull requests our customers open every day, not buried in a dashboard nobody checks

- Like problems with real weight: a multi-GB IPA, tens of thousands of screenshots in a single build, a binary format with sparse documentation

- Would rather own a feature from upload to UI than hand off half of it (end-to-end ownership)

- Enjoy building for developers, who will tell you exactly what’s wrong and why

- Want to help two products that started at a startup grow into core parts of Sentry

- 3+ years building production web services, with strong Python (Django preferred) and a habit of typed, tested code

- Working proficiency in React and TypeScript, enough to ship a full feature without handing off the frontend

- Experience with async task systems and event pipelines (Kafka, task queues, worker pools), including idempotency, locking, retries and their failure modes

- Experience with Postgres schema design and migrations that work under rolling deploys, plus pragmatic rollout habits like feature flags and revertable changes

- A track record of performance work: profiling, parallelism, memory reduction and large-file streaming through object storage

- Bonus points for:

- Hands-on experience with mobile build artifacts and tooling (LIEF, bundletool, apksigner, link maps, DWARF, code signing)

- Image processing or pixel-diff tooling

- GitHub Apps or the Checks API

- Data visualization, especially treemaps

- Prior work on developer tools, CI or observability products
